risks.note: MD&A section 6.1 states that presence across multiple service verticals 'helps reduce dependence on any single industry, customer segment, or revenue stream' and lets the Company balance market fluctuations in one segment with opportunities in others. Stated as a mitigation, it names the underlying exposure: earnings sit on a narrow set of verticals (Printing, Communication & Media, Record Management, Logistics & Cargo, Premium Mobility) and Printing Services is by far the largest of them, so a downturn in that one vertical is not offset by the smaller ones.
risks.risk: Dependence on any single industry, customer segment or revenue stream, which the diversified multi-vertical model is explicitly built to offset

risks.note: MD&A section 6.2 names the customer base as 'government institutions, BFSI clients, corporates, and other enterprise customers' and positions long-term relationships, service quality and customised solutions as the means to enhance 'customer retention'. Institutional and BFSI mandates are periodically re-tendered and price-competed; loss or non-renewal of a large institutional account is the single largest revenue event the Company describes itself as managing.
risks.risk: Client concentration in government institutions and BFSI enterprises, where relationships are contract/tender-based and retention is the stated defence

risks.note: MD&A section 6.3 places technology 'central to DJML's operations across document management, logistics, and business services' and commits continuing investment in 'digital platforms, information security measures, process automation, and employee awareness programmes to protect data'. The Corporate Overview repeats it as a core ESG/governance pillar ('robust data security frameworks', 'secure handling, transmission, and storage of critical information'). The Company physically and digitally holds client records for BFSI and government customers, so a breach is a client-loss and liability event, not just an IT incident.
risks.risk: Information-security and data-integrity risk from custody of third-party documents, records and communications

risks.note: MD&A section 6.4 says investments are 'evaluated through phased implementation and ongoing performance monitoring to ensure operational efficiency and effective utilisation of resources'. Phasing is a control on how fast capital is committed, not proof of demand behind it; utilisation shortfalls on new capacity would show first in margin, and FY26 EBITDA margin already moved down while revenue grew sharply.
risks.risk: Execution and capital-deployment risk on expansion, managed only by phasing rather than by committed contracts

risks.note: The Corporate Overview describes 'a shift from physical to digital ecosystems' through 'advanced digitization and document management solutions', and the ESG section lists 'paper reduction through digitization' as a key focus area in what it calls 'a resource-intensive industry'. The same trend that drives the Digitisation vertical erodes the Printing Solutions and physical Record Management volumes that currently carry the largest share of revenue; the transition has to be net-accretive, and the AR does not quantify the crossover.
risks.risk: Structural displacement of the physical-print and paper-based record verticals by the digitisation the Company itself sells

risks.note: The MD&A segment outlook table attributes Records Management to 'continued demand driven by compliance and information governance requirements' and Digitisation to 'digital transformation initiatives across sectors'. Demand created by a retention/compliance rule is durable while the rule stands but is exposed to a change in statutory retention periods or a regulator permitting digital-only custody, which would compress the physical storage business.
risks.risk: Regulation-driven demand: Record Management volumes rest on compliance and information-governance mandates rather than on customer discretionary spend

risks.note: In the MD&A segment-wise revenue disclosure, Logistics & Cargo Services was the sole vertical whose revenue fell year-on-year; every other vertical grew. Its stated outlook depends on 'infrastructure and trade expansion' - drivers outside the Company's control - so recovery in this vertical is not management-determined.
risks.risk: Logistics & Cargo was the only vertical to contract in FY26, while segment outlook ties it to external infrastructure and trade expansion

risks.note: The Board's report records that 'as on March 31, 2026, the Company had a subsidiary, namely Sai Links' and that a Policy for Determining Material Subsidiaries is in place; the segment disclosure shows Premium Mobility Services is carried entirely by Sailinks and is the second-largest vertical after Printing. Consolidated revenue therefore depends materially on one subsidiary whose vertical grew only marginally in FY26, and any governance, licensing or fleet issue there flows straight to consolidated results.
risks.risk: Dependence on the single material subsidiary Sai Links for the entire Premium Mobility vertical
